scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9058: Hello, I'm on PC0 (20.1.1.x). I can't get through to
PC12 (120.1.1.x) on the far side of the network any more -- it times out
every time. I vaguely remember hearing our two sides run on "different
routing" somehow, but I honestly don't know what that means. Could someone
take a look at whatever connects the two sides and fix it? Thanks a lot!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The OSPF core is converged, R11 redistributes
  between OSPF and EIGRP, and PC0 (20.1.1.x) reaches PC12 (120.1.1.x) with 0% loss
  in both directions. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of a redistribution / interior-link fault that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- PC0 cannot reach PC12
across the OSPF/EIGRP core -- is NOT reproducible: the OSPF backbone is converged,
R11 redistributes OSPF<->EIGRP (so the 120.x/EIGRP prefixes appear in the OSPF
RIB and vice versa), and PC0 reaches PC12 (120.1.1.x) with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: cross-core reachability is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the PC0->PC12
path, finds it working, optionally confirms R11's redistribution and the EIGRP
neighbors are up, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a broken
redistribution or a down interior link to satisfy the ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text: The user's report of PC0 (20.1.1.x) being unable to reach PC12 (120.1.1.x) is not confirmed by any live evidence. A topology-wide ICMP reachability sweep in Phase 1 shows 0% packet loss in both directions between the two hosts (RTT ≈ 1 ms). The network uses a split routing architecture: an OSPF domain covers r1–r10, and an EIGRP domain (AS 100) covers r12 and r13, with r11 acting as the redistribution boundary. r11 correctly runs both protocols — EIGRP with r12 (112.1.1.2, Full, 11+ min uptime) and r13 (103.1.1.2), and OSPF area 3 with r1 — and redistributes EIGRP routes (including 120.0.0.0/8) into OSPF and connected routes outbound. r1 carries a confirmed OSPF route to 120.0.0.0/8 via r11, and r12 holds a kernel default route covering the return path to 20.x. Phase A (infra_sweep, l2_snapshot) found no ACL rules, no MAC conflicts, and no addressing errors. Phase B tc_snapshot confirmed no traffic shaping. Phase D pressure_sweep found no stress tools or resource spikes. An ospf_snapshot flag on r8 (orphaned area 0.0.0.2) was investigated and found to be a correctly functioning leaf-stub area — r8 holds Full adjacencies with r5 (area 1) and r4 (via VLINK0, area 0), and its area-2 routes appear correctly in r1's routing table. No flap scripts, no carrier history, and no daemon logs indicate any intermittent mechanism. The user's complaint is unconfirmed; the current state is fully healthy.
